$comment: Stage-3 CASTING SLATE for NEW HARNOMY, U.S.A. Six candidates per principal. Lighting is held constant WITHIN each character so that candidates differ by face alone. Generated by build_casting_slate.py; regenerate after any kernel change.
framing_constant: medium close-up from the chest, straight-on to camera, plain neutral background, even exposure, the face at rest and not performing, no smile, no eyebrow lift, no dramatic gesture
legal_rule: Specify every character by age, origin, build, wardrobe, and affect only — never by likeness to a real public figure. If a render resembles a real person, regenerate.
how_to_judge: Compare within a character only. The six differ by face, not by light.
Read each character's test_question below before looking.
Reject anything resembling a real person (step 3.3) BEFORE choosing.
After picking four, run the silhouette test: all four at 40px, value only.
Summer's pick must also pass the portrait test before it locks.

valencia.role: Mezzo. The Greek chorus. The only character who tells the truth.
valencia.test_question: Do you believe she wants a manicure she cannot afford? The gap between what she is and what she wants to be IS the character.
valencia.trap: Two opposite failures. Cast her already beautiful and the wanting evaporates. Cast her as picturesque poverty and she becomes the working-class cosplay the opera is attacking. She is neither: she is a young woman with real calluses who would fix them tomorrow if she had the money.
valencia.lighting: flat honest documentary light, no sculpting, no glamour
valencia.canon_core: a young woman in her late twenties, slight build, direct steady eyes that assess before they answer, practical-length black hair, secondhand hipster layering worn as a work uniform rather than a statement - a thrifted cardigan over a plain tee, small cheap jewellery - visibly assembled from what was affordable rather than curated at expense, genuinely rough worked hands kept in frame, grooming attempted on a budget

summer.role: Soprano. The moral center. The hardest identity problem in the film.
summer.test_question: Can this face be glorified in a Socialist-Realist portrait AND freeze in horror beneath it? Too cold cannot be idealized; too warm cannot freeze.
summer.trap: She is Valencia's mirror. Valencia wants something she cannot afford; Summer has bought something she cannot return - she runs a reproductive-justice organization and had herself sterilized, and the Act III portrait glorifies her as a mother of the movement. None of that renders directly. What renders is that her stillness COSTS her something. A merely serene face has not understood the part.
summer.canon_core: a woman in her early forties, patrician bearing, slim and upright, a well-cut dark blazer over a fine plain knit in expensive unpatterned fabric, no logo, no jewellery beyond one minimal piece, a bare ring finger, hands completely still, composure that is visibly maintained rather than natural

pengold.role: Baritone. The machine. Carries two of the three load-bearing silences.
pengold.test_question: Is the face readable at rest? He opens on 22 seconds of silence and closes on the smallest possible smile.
pengold.trap: Two failures. A calculating face makes him a villain - he is not one, he is the intern who watched and learned, so the eyes read attentive, never scheming. And casting him smooth kills him: Dick's expensive clothes perform poverty, Pengold's perform belonging. Both are costumes; only Pengold knows it. The polish must look acquired.
pengold.canon_core: a man in his late forties, eyes that have been listening a long time, plain correct unshowy municipal suiting in dark muted wool, a white shirt, grooming a shade too precise - the correctness of a man who learned the rules rather than grew up inside them, heavy hands that did not come from an office, unhurried processional bearing

dick.role: Tenor. The sacrifice. His fall must land as pathos.
dick.test_question: Does the audience want to see him arrested? If yes, the ending does not work.
dick.trap: Punchability. The audience has to understand why Summer fell for him and why a bodega owner opened the door - so he must be genuinely likeable, which is not the same as handsome. He is the only principal whose face gives everything away, which is exactly why he never sees it coming. Note the rhyme with Valencia: near-identical silhouette, opposite bank balance. Hers is assembled from what was affordable; his is curated at expense to look that way.
dick.canon_core: a lean young man with an open unguarded face that gives everything away, immediately likeable, no wariness anywhere in it, the softness of someone who has never had to be hard, dark raw selvedge denim and a heritage workwear jacket over a faded band t-shirt, a handwoven scarf - the same silhouette a broke twenty-something would wear, bought at ten times the price
